nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space, $S \subseteq E$, $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $p \in E$. Then $\rho$ is a local defining function of $S$ at $p$ when $\rho(p) = 0$, $\rho$ is of class $C^2$ at $p$, its differential $D\rho(p)$ is nonzero, and for all $x$ in some neighborhood of $p$, $x \in S$ if and only if $\rho(x) = 0$. In particular $p \in S$.
nodes.title: Local defining function

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For all $a \in E$, $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $p \in E$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho(x) = \langle a, x \rangle - c$ through $p$ is $0$. In particular, for $a \neq 0$ the hyperplane $\{x \mid \langle a, x \rangle = c\}$ has mean curvature $0$ at each of its points.
nodes.title: Hyperplanes have zero mean curvature

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and every $p \in E$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $-\rho$ through $p$ is the negative of the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$: replacing $\rho$ by $-\rho$ reverses the unit normal and changes the sign of the mean curvature.
nodes.title: Reversing the normal negates the mean curvature

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$, every $p \in E$ and every real $c > 0$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $c\rho$ through $p$ equals the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$.
nodes.title: Positive rescaling preserves the mean curvature

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$, every $p \in E$ and every real $c \neq 0$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $c\rho$ through $p$ equals $c / |c|$ (the sign of $c$) times the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$.
nodes.title: Mean curvature under rescaling of the defining function

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$. For every $p \in E$ with $\|p\| = 1$, the mean curvature at $p$ of the level set of $\rho(x) = \|x\|^2 - 1$ through $p$ is $n - 1$. That is, the unit sphere of $E$ has mean curvature $n - 1$ with respect to the outward normal, the mean curvature being the sum (not the average) of the principal curvatures.
nodes.title: Mean curvature of the unit sphere

nodes.title: Mean curvature of a level set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space. For every $\rho : E \to \mathbb{R}$, all $p, u, v \in E$ and every real $c \neq 0$, the second fundamental form at $p$ of the level set of $c\rho$ through $p$, evaluated at $(u, v)$, equals $c / |c|$ (the sign of $c$) times the second fundamental form at $p$ of the level set of $\rho$ through $p$, evaluated at $(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Second fundamental form under rescaling of the defining function

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
